clue.text: Outcry caused by VIP

definitions.meaning: an outcry is a loud public clamour, literally a great din
a very important person is informally called a bigwig or big shot

explanation.surface: A celebrity's arrival sparks a public uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit the phrase: a loud clamour is literally a large sound, and an important person is idiomatically one too.

clue.text: Bear East to Grantchester to find his old lodgings

definitions.text: Grantchester to find his old lodgings

parts.note: to brook something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A poet heads east to the village where he once lived.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet Rupert Brooke lived at Grantchester, a village near Cambridge; the definition is a loose allusion to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edwardian poet lodged in that Cambridgeshire village and wrote a famous poem about it.

clue.text: General Secretary takes in brewed beer for the birds

indicators.note: one piece receiving another means the second goes inside it

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for general
S is an abbreviation for secretary

indicators.note: brewing works the ingredients over, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A senior official drinks home-made ale while watching wildfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' signals the anagram of the drink, and 'takes in' wraps the abbreviations for General and Secretary around it; 'for' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are diving waterfowl, a family of water birds.

clue.text: Love friends! They re gems

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
pals are friends

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising one's dear friends as treasures.
explanation.definitionFit: These are iridescent precious stones, a kind of gem.

clue.text: Shilling needed to be paid to view performance

parts.note: sh is an old abbreviation for shilling, a pre-decimal British coin
money owing is still due

explanation.surface: Admission to a show costs a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin worth twelve pence; SH is an older abbreviation for it than the usual S. 'to view' sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A screening of a film or a staged presentation is a performance.

clue.text: Begging to be regarded like royalty

parts.note: like means as, in the sense of in the manner of
a king is a member of royalty

explanation.surface: Someone pleading for favour hopes to be treated like a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for alms is begging; the participle matches the clue's -ing form.

clue.text: Made disorderly haste over rough ground

definitions.text: Made disorderly haste over rough ground

parts.words: Made disorderly haste over rough ground
parts.note: describes clambering hurriedly over uneven terrain, while also hinting at mixing things up

explanation.surface: Someone hurried clumsily across uneven terrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamber hastily over rocky terrain is the core sense, which also means jumbled.

clue.text: Where fighting soldiers may be found doing nothing

definitions.text: Where fighting soldiers may be found
definitions.meaning: soldiers engaged in combat are said to be in battle, read as two words

explanation.surface: Troops in battle contrasted with idle ones.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means engaged in combat; as one word it means idleness.

clue.text: Produce green tea

annotationWithheld.why: Produce green tea (8): the only parse makes 'Produce' both the definition and the anagram indicator for GREEN TEA, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: He manages to become a surgeon

definitions.meaning: one who runs or works a business or machine
a surgeon is one who operates on patients

explanation.surface: A manager aspires to retrain in medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person running a concern and, informally, a surgeon who performs operations.

clue.text: Decree that Noraid be disbanded

indicators.note: a disbanded group is broken up, so the letters of the organisation's name are scattered and regrouped

explanation.surface: An order goes out that an Irish-American fundraising group be broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be disbanded' rearranges NORAID. Noraid was an American group that raised funds for Irish republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order something officially, the same as to decree it as a verb.

clue.text: They offer poor support to a former railway company

parts.note: LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a British company before nationalisation

explanation.surface: Contributors give little backing to an old rail firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor support' looks like weak backing; it means support for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts of money or food help the needy.

clue.text: Make no move to retain ownership of a whisky manufactory

parts.note: to keep something is to go on owning it
a still is the apparatus or distillery where whisky is made

explanation.surface: Someone advised to hold on to their whisky distillery rather than act.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay motionless is the plain sense of the phrase, an idiom for not moving.

clue.text: Doctor gets to the river by car

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A doctor drives down to the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor is a dated British word for an automobile.

clue.text: Vessel given by the Colonel's superior

definitions.meaning: short for brigadier, the army rank above colonel

explanation.surface: A ship is handed over by a senior army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sailing ship and is also the informal short form of brigadier, outranking a colonel.

clue.text: He acts without principle when about to get a will verified

parts.note: re means about or concerning
probate is the official proving of a will

explanation.surface: A rogue is about to have a will proved.
explanation.definitionFit: An unprincipled scoundrel behaves with no morals.

clue.text: No more tickets left? It's a betrayal

definitions.meaning: an event whose tickets are all gone is a complete sale
selling out one's side means betraying it

explanation.surface: A concert sells all its seats, but someone calls it treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sold-out event has no seats remaining, and selling out a cause is treachery.

clue.text: Precisely when to make them wait?

definitions.text: Precisely when to make them wait?

parts.words: Precisely when to make them wait?
parts.note: asks for the exact moment, a demonstrative phrase pointing at a particular occasion

explanation.surface: Someone asks exactly when to keep people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrative phrase pinpoints a particular occasion, exactly when.

clue.text: I'd set up a measurement-gauge in the central line

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting the word up means reading it backwards

parts.note: a meter is a measuring instrument

explanation.surface: Someone installs a measuring gauge in a middle line.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight line through the centre of a circle is its chord through the middle.

clue.text: Neat little lock-keeper

parts.note: not a canal official but a small tidy device that holds a lock of hair in place

explanation.surface: A tidy small man runs a canal lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-keeper' suggests canal staff; the lock is a strand of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin for the hair holds a tress of hair, so it is a small holder of curls.

clue.text: Standard denial by the Marines

parts.note: no is a denial
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: The Marines refuse to meet a standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A usual benchmark or level is a standard.

clue.text: They help to identify a grave complaint initially

definitions.meaning: the initials of acquired immune deficiency syndrome, a serious disease

explanation.surface: Diagnostic tools that help doctors pin down a serious illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Helpers are supports, and the same letters are the acronym of a grave immune-system illness.

clue.text: Can I be of a pleasant disposition

definitions.meaning: read as three words the letters ask ..., which means can I

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if they can be good-natured.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured, split as three words it asks whether one is capable.

clue.text: Just the chair for the one who cuts the joint

definitions.meaning: an armchair at the head of a dining table

definitions.text: the one who cuts the joint
definitions.meaning: a person who slices roast meat

explanation.surface: A dining chair suited to whoever slices the roast.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed dining chair is so named, and so is a person slicing meat.

clue.text: Ruined, broken and hardened

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone ruined and broken becomes tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed to hardship so as to feel it less, toughened.

clue.text: Time when a freelance secretary has nothing

parts.note: a temp is an agency secretary hired for short spells
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: An agency typist turns up with no work to do.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the speed or pace at which a piece is played is its time.

clue.text: Bring up the question of original fratricide and cause chaos

parts.note: to raise a matter is to bring it up for discussion
in Genesis Cain killed his brother Abel, the first murder of a brother

explanation.surface: Mentioning the Bible's first brother-killing leads to uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make a great fuss or uproar, creating disorder.

clue.text: Choose out of a selection of parties

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Voters pick from a range of political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To vote for or pick someone is to choose them.

clue.text: Where to find letter calling for explanation after train-crash

indicators.note: the explanation-seeking letter is placed after the wrecked train letters
a train crash wrecks the carriages, so the letters of the word are thrown about

parts.note: Y sounds like why, the question that asks for an explanation

explanation.surface: A letter demanding an account of a railway disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' signals the anagram of the train, and 'after' places the explanation-seeking letter last. 'letter' here means post, not an alphabet character.
explanation.definitionFit: Incoming mail awaiting attention sits in a tray on an office desk.

clue.text: One who looks at a Sunday paper

explanation.surface: Someone reading a weekend newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is one who observes, and a long-running British weekend newspaper bears the same title.

clue.text: Organ donated to Edward and it's well deserved

parts.note: the ear is an organ of the body
Ned is a pet form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A transplant goes to a man called Edward, who merits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gained through effort and merit is rightly deserved.

clue.text: Retail establishment goes into the red after having repairs done

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: red is taken as written
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: A shop falls into debt after being refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes into' places the shop inside the colour; 'the red' in the surface suggests debt, but here it just gives its three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repaired has been brought back to its former condition.
